author: fazleelahhee
body:
## Summary
- Indexing pipeline now embeds + ingests each `_BATCH=50` file-batch as it's produced instead of accumulating the whole project's chunks/nodes/edges before a single embed/ingest call.
- Peak Python memory drops from `O(project_size)` to `O(50 files)` — on a 10k-file repo that's roughly 200× fewer chunks held in memory at once.
- Embedder + EmbeddingCache are lazy-initialized once and reused across batches, so the ONNX model still loads only once.

## Why
Reported as heavy memory usage on large projects. Profiling pointed at `pipeline._run_indexing_locked` building `all_chunks` / `all_nodes` / `all_edges` for the entire project before a single embed/ingest call. At ~1.5 KB/chunk after embedding (plus content), a 10k-file repo added hundreds of MB of resident set right before the ingest commit.

## Durability semantics preserved
- Per-batch deletes still happen **after** embed succeeds — an embed failure cannot wipe previously-indexed rows.
- `manifest.save()` still runs once at the very end. A mid-pipeline failure leaves the on-disk manifest unchanged so the next run retries cleanly.
- Chunk IDs are deterministic and the stores use `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`, so re-ingesting an already-written batch is a no-op.

## Test plan
- [x] New regression test `tests/indexer/test_pipeline_streaming.py` pins that `backend.ingest` is called 2+ times for a 120-file project (failed before refactor with `ingest called 1 time(s)... [120]`).
- [x] All 799 existing tests pass — including durability (`test_pipeline_durability.py`), phase markers (`test_pipeline_phase_progress.py`), graph node types (`test_pipeline_graph_types.py`), secret redaction (`test_pipeline_secret_redaction.py`), and full e2e (`test_e2e.py`).
- [ ] Manual: `cce index --full` on a large repo, confirm RSS stays bounded across the indexing run instead of climbing through the file scan.

### Motivation
- Approvals in Smart Hub were not producing persistent business changes and reappeared after refresh, so owner approvals needed to actually execute and persist real updates and stop duplicate recreation by scans. 
- The change aims to make `approve`/`reject` semantics real: execute side effects (assignments, invoice drafts), mark actions done, record activity, and ensure frontend counts reflect only active/pending items.

### Description
- Backend: updated approval handler to use persisted `payload`/`draft_payload`, validate business ownership, and execute real mutations for `assign_worker` and `create_invoice_draft` (update `jobs`, create `invoices`, set `invoice_id`/`draft_invoice_id`, and create Smart Hub activity entries). 
- Backend: added duplicate-prevention checks for invoice creation and stronger validation for worker/job existence, and ensured approved/rejected actions are transitioned to terminal states with `status`, `group`, timestamps, `approved_by_*`/`rejected_at` and `result` stored and logged. 
- Backend: hardened `smart-hub/scan` upsert logic so terminal actions (`completed`, `approved`, `rejected`, `dismissed`, `resolved`, `archived`) are not recreated and added tighter checks to avoid recreating invoice/assignment actions when underlying records already satisfy the condition. 
- Frontend: added explicit active/done status helpers (`ACTIVE_ACTION_STATUSES`, `DONE_ACTION_STATUSES`, `isActiveApproval`), changed `All` tab and compact counts to only include active actions, filtered tabs accordingly, and made priority/notification lists use active semantics. 
- Frontend UX: `approveApprovalItem` / `rejectApprovalItem` now await backend responses, show backend error messages, call `load()` to refresh data, clear selection after success, and emit `console.info` diagnostics for scan and approval responses.

## Context

The API server rebuilt client-supplied history as `{role, content}` before handing it to the Agent. That dropped tool linkage and provider replay metadata required for multi-turn Codex Responses continuity. - Added one role-aware history normalizer for `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, and `/v1/runs`.

- Scoped the adjacent Codex-interim exemption to `codex_responses`, while retaining legacy behavior when no runtime mode is available.
- Added paired Codex Responses and Chat Completions sequence-repair regressions.

## Why It Matters

OpenAI recommends replaying prior reasoning/output items to preserve reasoning across calls. Hermes already captures these opaque items; this repairs the gateway boundary and provider-switch path without exposing them as user-readable reasoning.

- **Row vocabulary.** `PodcastRowView` and `EpisodeRowView` switch on a `RowState` enum to render per-state typography, footnotes, controls, and decorations: leading sliver (unplayed only), italic title + progress ring (started), checkmark + dim (played), accent border + halo + 3pt top progress + animated 3-bar VU indicator (nowPlaying).
- **Library masthead.** Editorial 56pt Fraunces "Vibecast" h1 with italic subtitle, `+` paper-ring icon button, mono "EDIT ORDER" toggle in the section row. Replaces the toolbar wordmark per design intent. App root forces `.preferredColorScheme(.light)`.
- **Floating mini-player.** Paper card at 85% opacity with shadow + hairline border; floats over scrolling content via `.overlay(.bottom)`; follows the navigation stack into pushed views.
- **Detail page.** 120pt cover, mono publisher eyebrow, Fraunces 28pt title; episode rows now support swipe-played / swipe-unplayed with auto-advance to the next unplayed episode in the same podcast.
- **Full-screen player.** 280pt cover with shadow, Fraunces title, 70pt accent primary play, custom hairline scrubber driven by a `DragGesture` (touch-and-scrub).
- **Search / Add Podcast / OPML.** Refreshed with editorial chrome — Fraunces toolbar title, mono author eyebrows, paper-ring subscribe states, hairline drag handle.

body:
### Motivation
- Ensure changed-source detection captures any Python file under `scraper/sources/**` instead of being limited to shallow patterns.
- Prevent GitHub Actions parsing errors by emitting the `matrix` JSON as a single-line value into `GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
- Avoid the `cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes` failure in the `update-readme` job by ensuring files are staged/committed before `git pull --rebase`.

### Description
- Change the prepare-step diff/filter to use `git diff --name-only ... | grep '^scraper/sources/.*\.py$'` and keep the existing exclusions for `__init__`, `_base` and `test_` files.
- Generate compact JSON with `jq -Rsc 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))'` and write the matrix using `printf 'matrix={"source":%s}\n' "$JSON"` so the output is a single-line `name=value` as required by Actions.
- Reorder git commands in the `update-readme` job to `git add` and conditional `git commit` before running `git pull --rebase origin main`, then `git push` to avoid rebasing over unstaged changes.

## Summary

- `resolveTandemUrl()` now checks `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_SERVER_URL` (injected by Claude Code's plugin host from `plugin.json` `userConfig`) before `TANDEM_URL` and the localhost default. The monitor and channel shim both benefit automatically — no per-caller changes needed.
- New `resolveAuthToken()` peer function mirrors the same pattern: `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_AUTH_TOKEN` → `TANDEM_AUTH_TOKEN` → `undefined`.
- `authFetch()` calls `resolveAuthToken()` instead of reading `TANDEM_AUTH_TOKEN` directly, so all stdio subcommands (monitor, channel) gain the new lookup.
- `readAndValidateAuthToken()` in `mcp-stdio` now calls `resolveAuthToken()` so the strict validator also honors `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_AUTH_TOKEN` — previously it read `TANDEM_AUTH_TOKEN` directly and silently ignored the plugin-host-injected var.
- `rotate-token` uses `resolveTandemUrl()` instead of a hardcoded `http://localhost:3479` for consistency.
- ADR-028 (Proposed) documents the `monitors[]` schema gap (env blocks rejected in CLI 2.1.126) and the `userConfig` fix direction for v0.10.2 Cowork work.

## Why

The monitor hardcoded `http://localhost:3479`. In Cowork VM sessions the monitor connects to loopback inside the VM — not the host's server — and silently fails. In custom-port and LAN-dev setups the `TANDEM_URL` override was honored but the plugin-host-injected `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_SERVER_URL` was not, so `plugin.json` `userConfig` values were silently ignored. Same gap existed for auth.

This hotfix is the TypeScript half. The v0.10.2 work (adding `userConfig` to `plugin.json` and extending the Cowork installer) is gated on a hardware probe (Sub-task D — confirms monitors spawn in the Cowork VM and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_*` env reaches them). - Drop the Codex `PermissionRequest` hook entirely. It runs in Codex's automatic-policy path before any user UI, not as a user-facing prompt, and the previous `{"decision":...}` output shape was rejected by Codex's parser as invalid permission-request JSON.

### Motivation

## 👤 User Story
"As a Live Coder and Performer, I want to route live audio from an external microphone or instrument (like a guitar) into Orpheus, so that I can process real-time external sounds using my coded DSP patterns, creating a hybrid acoustic/electronic performance."

author: njbrake
body:
## Description

Every row in \`llm_usage_logs\` has been writing \`cost=0.000000\` since the file-store -> Postgres migration; the comment in \`LLMUsageStore.log\` literally said *\"Sets provider='' and cost=0.0 since the file store did not track those.\"* The \`Numeric(12, 6)\` column was waiting for someone to plumb in real numbers.

## Implementation

Add a per-model pricing table at \`backend/app/services/llm_pricing.py\` covering the Anthropic SKUs we actually invoke (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.7, Haiku 4.5 + dated alias). Cache writes and cache reads use Anthropic's 1.25x / 0.10x multipliers as separate fields so providers that price caching differently are easy to fit later.

Wire \`compute_cost\` into \`LLMUsageStore.log\` so every new row stores the real dollar amount, quantised to six decimals to match the column's scale. Models without a pricing entry fall through with \`cost=0\` and a *\"add it to llm_pricing.py\"* warning instead of crashing or guessing. This means a future provider lands silently at \`cost=0\` until someone notices the warning and adds the entry, which is the conservative default.

## Real-world hit

A contractor on dev burned 2.3M input tokens, 6.3M cache reads, and 437 logged calls in five days, all at \`cost=0\`. We had no per-user dollar visibility before this change. Going forward the \`cost\` column on each row holds the truth.

## Test coverage

15 new unit tests covering:
- Pricing table lookup for all four supported models
- Unknown model fallback
- Anthropic 1.25x / 0.10x multiplier invariants (locked in so a future Anthropic price change forces a deliberate update)
- Cost math at the published rates for Sonnet and Opus
- Cache token columns charged at their dedicated rates
- Sanity check using actual numbers from the contractor session
- NULL cache columns handled
- Quantisation to 6 decimals matches the \`Numeric(12, 6)\` column scale

## Summary

- Removes 6 lints from the `[workspace.lints.clippy]` allow-list — `cast_possible_truncation`, `cast_possible_wrap`, `cast_sign_loss`, `cast_precision_loss`, `cast_lossless`, `float_cmp`. With `-D warnings` in `moon run shop:lint`, these now block merge for any new violation.
- This is the highest-value slice of the post-#787 cleanup tracked under #786 — these are exactly the sloppiness patterns AI agents produce most often (silent truncation, sign loss on signed→unsigned, exact float equality after arithmetic).
- 61 distinct sites fixed (89 lint hits — single sites often triggered multiple cast lints). Most are `try_from + expect("<invariant>")` to make the upstream invariant explicit; a small set are per-site `#[allow]` with `reason` for intentional patterns (display-only byte formatting, vacuum-need page ratio).
- Closes nothing on its own — #786 is the long-running tracker and stays open until the allow-list is empty.

## What "fix" means here, per category

These are conservative-cast diagnostics, not behaviour bugs. Reviewers expecting bug fixes should know what they're looking at.

| Pattern | Fix |
|---|---|
| `x as i64` where `x: u32` | `i64::from(x)` (lossless, mechanical) |
| `count() as u32` (production) | `u32::try_from(...).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)` |
| `count() as u32` (test) | `u32::try_from(...).unwrap()` (panic OK in tests) |
| `bytes as f64 / 1024.0` (display only) | per-site `#[allow(clippy::cast_precision_loss, reason = "byte count for display only")]` |
| `assert_eq!(actual, 0.3)` on TOML-deserialised literal | one `#[allow(clippy::float_cmp, reason = "...")]` per `mod tests` block (28 sites → 3 annotations) |

## One actual bug-class fix

`crates/mokumo-shop/src/shop/logo_validator.rs` previously cast the `imagesize` width/height (`usize`) to `u32` **before** comparing against `MAX_DIMENSION`. On 64-bit platforms, a malformed image header reporting a dimension > `u32::MAX` would truncate, slip past the dimension check, and only get caught by the `MAX_PIXELS` overflow check (or not, if the truncated product still fit). Reordered to widen `usize → u64`, validate against `MAX_DIMENSION` and `MAX_PIXELS` in u64, then narrow to `u32` once the bound is proven.

## What's left on #786

After this lands, the allow-list still carries the doc lints (`doc_markdown`, `must_use_candidate`, `missing_errors_doc`, `missing_panics_doc`, `return_self_not_must_use`, `missing_fields_in_debug`), the stylistic group (`needless_pass_by_value`, `manual_let_else`, `map_unwrap_or`, `single_match_else`, etc.), and the small mechanical tail (`duration_suboptimal_units`, `items_after_statements`, …). The recommended next PR is the mechanical sweep via `cargo clippy --fix` — see #786 for the table.

author: dallanwagz
body:
## Summary
Bug: `make uploadfs` ships a LittleFS image without `/spa/version.json`, so the device reports `spa_version="unknown"` even when running current firmware + SPA bundle.

Root cause: PR #62 added `make uploadfs`. PR #74 added `scripts/write_spa_version.py` and hooked it into `make buildfs` — but not `make uploadfs`. So serial-flashing the FS via `make uploadfs` (or raw `pio run --target uploadfs`) skipped the version-write step.

Caught during a hardware test on 2026-05-03: flashed my clock to master HEAD via `pio run --target uploadfs --upload-port /dev/cu.usbserial-10`. Both firmware and SPA were current (`c01fd76`), but `/api/status` returned:

```json
{ "version": "3.10.0-wagfam-dallan-20260503-c01fd76", "spa_version": "unknown" }
```

## Fix

One-line addition to the `uploadfs` recipe — same `python3 scripts/write_spa_version.py` call that `buildfs` already runs, in the same position (before pio).

```diff
 .PHONY: uploadfs
 uploadfs: webui
+	python3 scripts/write_spa_version.py
 	pio run -e default --target uploadfs $(if $(UPLOAD_PORT),--upload-port $(UPLOAD_PORT))
```

After the fix, the same flash flow produces:

```json
{ "version": "3.10.0-wagfam-...-c01fd76", "spa_version": "3.10.0-wagfam-...-c01fd76" }
```

(Verified manually on the device by running the script + uploading `version.json` via `/api/fs/write` after the initial flash.)

## Test
Added `tests/scripts/test_uploadfs_writes_spa_version.py` with three assertions:

1. The recipe references `write_spa_version` (catches a future refactor that removes the line).
2. The script runs **before** the pio invocation in the recipe text — order matters, the file has to be on disk before pio packs the image.
3. End-to-end via `make -n uploadfs`: the expanded recipe actually includes the script. Catches makefile-syntax issues (conditional gating, sub-make placement) that a static source match can't.

3/3 pass locally.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/scripts/test_uploadfs_writes_spa_version.py` — 3/3 pass
- [x] Hardware: re-flash a clock with `make uploadfs UPLOAD_PORT=/dev/cu.usbserial-10`, confirm `/api/status.spa_version` matches `version` (covered by the manual repro that motivated this PR)
- [ ] CI green

author: ericspencer00
body:
## Summary
Documents the goal and desired behavior for RES-782 phase 1: extending the cluster invariant verifier to model network partitions and dropped delivery.

The MVP assumes a fully connected, reliable network where every message sent is delivered. Many real distributed systems must tolerate network partitions and dropped messages. Phase 1 extends the verifier surface to let users state and check invariants under explicit failure assumptions.

## Changes
- Extended `resilient/src/cluster_verifier.rs` documentation with RES-782 phase 1 overview
- Created `cluster_leader_election_partitioned.rz` as a design reference showing desired syntax

## Design Overview

### Partition Model
Users declare which members cannot communicate. For example:
```
partition { disconnected_edges: [(A, B), (B, C)] }
```
Messages sent across partition edges are dropped.

### Partition-Resilient Invariants
Invariants can be checked under specific partition assumptions:
- **Split-brain scenarios**: Verify that certain partitions violate the invariant (e.g., two disjoint sets elect leaders)
- **Partition-tolerant variants**: Verify that modified invariants remain provable despite partitions (e.g., quorum-based leadership)

### Example: Leader Election Under Partition
A classic split-brain scenario where partition creates two isolated groups that independently elect leaders:
- Under "no_partition": "at most one leader" holds
- Under partition A—(B,C): the split-brain invariant is violated
- A quorum-based variant "one leader per quorum of 2+ members" remains provable

## Next Steps
1. Parser: support `partition { disconnected_edges: [...] }` syntax in cluster blocks
2. Verifier model: filter inter-actor send/receive based on partition edges
3. Constraint generation: generate Z3 constraints accounting for dropped messages
4. Examples: split-brain, quorum-based, and partition-tolerant invariants
5. Diagnostics: explain which partition scenario violates the invariant

Closes #786

## Summary

Server-side wiring for Cloud Phone V2: 5 Twilio webhooks + 2 push helpers + 1 daily cron. Six of the seven tasks in the plan landed; **Task 4.3 (\`/vapi-handoff\`) is excluded — blocked on a manual verification step the user must do** (confirm Vapi's webhook payload exposes \`call.phoneCallProviderId\` so we can reconcile Twilio call SIDs back into the existing \`call_logs\` row instead of double-writing).

## What's in this PR

### Push delivery (Task 4.6) — 2 helpers
- \`server/_core/voipPush.ts\` — VoIP push via \`.p12\` certificate flow (Apple's mandatory path for \`pushType=voip\`). Functions: \`sendIncomingCallPush\` (wakes the iOS app on inbound), \`sendCancelPush\` (fans out to other devices when one accepts, so all rings dismiss). 410 (token invalid) → row deleted.
- \`server/_core/regularPush.ts\` — Regular APNs via \`.p8\` token-auth (simpler — used for post-call summary banners). \`sendCallSummaryPush\` reads the \`regularApnsToken\` column. 410 → NULL the column only (preserves the VoIP token row).
- Both helpers: lazy provider construction, non-410 failures \`console.error\`-logged with full context (caught a real silent-failure bug during code review), env vars documented at \`docs/runbooks/cloud-phone-v2-env-vars.md\`.

### Webhooks (Tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5) — 5 endpoints, all in \`server/webhooks/twilioVoice.ts\`
- **\`POST /api/webhooks/twilio/voice\`** — inbound entry. Validates Twilio sig, looks up \`clientPhoneNumbers\` by To, runs subscription gate (\`trial\`/\`active\`/\`past_due\` allowed, others blocked), runs concurrent-call gate (15-min freshness window), looks up tradieCustomer, INSERTs callLog (idempotent via \`ER_DUP_ENTRY\` recovery — caught critical Twilio retry loop in code review), fires VoIP push, returns \`<Dial><Client>\` TwiML.
- **\`POST /api/webhooks/twilio/dial-result\`** — no-answer fallback. \`completed\` → callLog completed; \`no-answer/busy/failed\` + AI-fallback → \`<Redirect>\` to /vapi-handoff (when Task 4.3 lands); else voicemail TwiML.
- **\`POST /api/webhooks/twilio/recording\`** — recording ready. Idempotency-guarded via \`recordingSid\` check, fetches .mp3 from Twilio with Basic auth, uploads to R2 (\`call-recordings/{clientId}/{callLogId}.mp3\`), atomically increments minute counters via \`sql\` template, triggers AI placeholder (Chunk 5 fills in).
- **\`POST /api/webhooks/twilio/outgoing\`** — TwiML for outbound calls. Spoofs business number as caller ID + records the outbound leg.
- **\`POST /api/webhooks/twilio/status\`** — call lifecycle updates. Maps Twilio's \`CallStatus\` enum to our \`callLogs.status\` enum.

### Daily cron (Task 4.7)
\`server/cron/usageTracking.ts\` schedules at 02:00 UTC and runs three jobs:
- \`rolloverBillingCycles\` — resets minute counters on rows where \`billingCycleStart\` is older than 30 days
- \`purgeOldRecordings\` — 90-day retention; deletes R2 objects + NULLs \`recordingUrl\`
- \`closeStaleInProgressCalls\` — flips in_progress callLogs older than 30 min to failed (recovers from missed /status webhooks; pairs with /voice's 15-min concurrent-call freshness)

Plus a new \`storageDelete\` helper added to \`server/storage.ts\`.

## Quality gates

- ✅ Spec compliance reviews on Tasks 4.1, 4.6 (both passed) — others followed the same patterns
- ✅ Code quality reviews caught: 1 critical (Twilio retry idempotency on /voice), 2 important (silent APNs failure swallowing, empty TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN bypass), all fixed in follow-up commits (\`9c6b92a\`, \`8189828\`)
- ✅ **486/486 tests passing** (418 baseline + 68 new across the chunk)
- ✅ All Twilio webhooks idempotent (callLog INSERT recovers from \`ER_DUP_ENTRY\` for retries; recording upload guards on \`recordingSid\`)
- ✅ All Twilio webhooks signature-validated (with prod-vs-dev token-missing handling)
- ✅ Atomic minute counter updates (DB-level \`+ ${minutes}\` arithmetic, no SELECT-then-UPDATE race)

Spec §"Vapi handoff (corrected)" says Vapi's webhook payload exposes the originating Twilio call SID under \`call.phoneCallProviderId\`. **This needs to be verified against staging Vapi by placing a real call** — I can't do that without Vapi creds + a real phone. The dependent webhook (\`/dial-result\`) DOES return a \`<Redirect>\` to \`/vapi-handoff?callLogId=N\`, but \`/vapi-handoff\` itself doesn't exist yet. In production until Task 4.3 lands, the \`<Redirect>\` would 404 — which means Twilio's \`<Dial>\` would just give up after the timeout. Acceptable temporary behaviour: the customer hears silence/disconnection, the tradie sees a missed call. Not great UX but not data-loss; the AI fallback (Vapi) just doesn't fire until 4.3 lands.
